newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine parl to debate tax laws in a week - Speaker.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine parl to debate tax laws in a week - Speaker.

text.p: Ukraine's parliament will debate within a week three key tax reform laws, part of a package of nine tax reform laws which would form the basis of the delayed 1997 budget, deputy speaker Alexander Tkachenko said on Wednesday.

"If by next Wednesday we can debate the laws on profits earned by citizens, on changes to existing laws to make them comply with new tax rules, and on profits earned by businesses, this would allow parliament to accept the 1997 budget by the end of April," Tkachenko told parliament.

Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko earlier this month urged deputies to accept at least four of the nine tax laws, without which it would be impossible to implement the 1997 budget. Only a new law on value-added tax has been passed so far.
The budget has been stuck between government and parliament, and if accepted would pave the way for Ukraine's receipt of a $2.5 to $3 billion, three-year Extended Fund Facility (EFF).

President Leonid Kuchma said last week the new budget and tax laws, even if accepted this month or next, could not be implemented until at least July and that Ukraine would have to continue operating with last year's budget.
